items.title: Some Simple Economics of AGI
items.desc: arXiv (econ). Builds a tractable framework for reasoning about the macroeconomic consequences of artificial general intelligence, including its effects on growth, wages, and factor shares.

items.title: Predictive Economics: Rethinking Economic Methodology with Machine Learning
items.desc: arXiv (econ.GN). Argues for treating prediction as a first-class objective in economics and examines how machine-learning methods reshape economic methodology alongside traditional causal inference.

items.title: Using Machine Learning to Generate, Clarify, and Improve Economic Models
items.desc: arXiv (econ). Explores how ML systems can help economists propose, refine, and stress-test formal economic models rather than only estimate existing ones.

items.title: Automation, AI, and the Intergenerational Transmission of Knowledge
items.desc: arXiv (econ.GN). Studies how AI-driven automation affects how skills and knowledge pass between generations of workers, and the long-run implications for human capital.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Asset Pricing Models
items.desc: Kelly, Kuznetsov, Malamud & Xu (NBER WP 33351). Develops asset-pricing models built on modern AI/deep-learning architectures and studies their out-of-sample performance relative to classical factor models.

items.title: Empirical Asset Pricing with Large Language Model Agents
items.desc: arXiv (q-fin). Uses LLM-based agents to form return forecasts and construct portfolios, testing whether language-model reasoning adds signal in empirical asset pricing.

items.title: Integrating Large Language Models in Financial Investments and Market Analysis: A Survey
items.desc: arXiv (q-fin). Surveys how LLMs are being applied across investment research, market analysis, and trading, and catalogs the main opportunities and open challenges.

items.title: Auditing Asset-Specific Preferences in Financial Large Language Models
items.desc: arXiv (q-fin). Probes financial LLMs for embedded asset-specific biases (e.g., toward Bitcoin) and shows how such preferences can distort portfolio-allocation advice.

items.title: A Comprehensive Review of AI-Driven Credit Risk Modeling: From Traditional Scoring to Explainable Machine Learning
items.desc: Gates & Flynn (SSRN). Reviews the shift from traditional credit scoring to modern, explainable ML approaches in banking, weighing accuracy gains against transparency and governance.

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: Can Deep Reinforcement Learning Improve Inventory Management? Performance on Lost Sales, Dual-Sourcing, and Multi-Echelon Problems
items.desc: M&SOM. Benchmarks deep reinforcement learning against established heuristics across canonical inventory problems, assessing where learned policies genuinely help.

items.title: Personalized Dynamic Pricing with Machine Learning: High-Dimensional Features and Heterogeneous Elasticity
items.desc: Management Science. Develops an ML pricing method that exploits high-dimensional customer features and heterogeneous price sensitivity to set personalized prices.

items.title: A Manager and an AI Walk into a Bar: Does ChatGPT Make Biased Decisions Like We Do?
items.desc: M&SOM. Tests ChatGPT on 18 operations-relevant human biases and finds it mirrors human bias in roughly half of the experiments while diverging in the rest.

items.title: A Deep Q-Network for the Beer Game: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Inventory Optimization
items.desc: M&SOM. Applies a deep Q-network to the classic Beer Game supply-chain setting, learning ordering policies that reduce the bullwhip effect.

items.title: Large Language Models in Creative Work: The Role of Collaboration Modality and User Expertise
items.desc: Management Science. Field/experimental evidence on how LLM collaboration modality and user expertise shape the quality and value of AI-assisted creative and knowledge work.

items.title: AI has taken over the stock market. The bond market is next
items.desc: The Economist (Jul 7). Meta, Nvidia, Oracle, SpaceX and Amazon have each raised tens of billions in AI-linked bonds; Morgan Stanley expects $350-400bn of AI investment-grade issuance in America this year, and the BIS warns some AI projects may not earn enough to repay it.

items.title: China's semiconductor industry is racing to catch the West's
items.desc: The Economist (Jul 7). On China's accelerating push to close the gap in advanced chipmaking that underpins the AI race, and what it means for the global tech supply chain.

items.title: From Cow-Milking Robots to Weed-Zapping Lasers, Farmers Are Embracing A.I.
items.desc: NYT (Jun 5). How AI and robotics are moving into agricultural operations, from autonomous milking to laser weeding, reshaping farm labor and productivity.
